supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS alert is consistent with the inventory-listed ChartMate updater: cmupdate.exe started at 13:37:41, and proxy CONNECTs to update.chartmate-imaging.com recur from 13:37:44 through 14:07:42 at roughly five-minute intervals. The corresponding network events show the workstation connecting through the explicit proxy.

Explorer recorded a UserAssist path that decodes from ROT13 to C:\Windows\System32\mstsc.exe at 14:10:23. This is a notable remote-desktop-related artifact, but the record does not itself establish a process launch or a remote session.

The workstation made SMB connections to DC-HD-01 at 13:33 and 14:10, with associated domain machine-account authentication. These records do not identify the accessed shares or show what activity occurred over SMB.
Sysmon recorded svchost.exe accessing LSASS with GrantedAccess 0x1400 at 13:21 and 0x1000 at 14:03. The records do not identify the svchost service or show LSASS memory being read.
The records show browser access to Reddit and a Firefox launch targeting docs.google.com; they do not show that files were uploaded or that data was exfiltrated.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor status reports winsec and Sysmon collection outages for WS-LPARK-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC. Those outages are for a different host; the supplied status says collection was OK for other hosts, including WS-BCARTER-01.
Proxy records identify CONNECT hostnames and proxy tunnels, but the provided evidence does not include the HTTPS payloads.
The provided SMB connection records do not include share names or file-operation details.
claims_not_established: That the ChartMate updater traffic was malicious or represented command-and-control rather than the approved update check.
That mstsc.exe was actually launched, connected to a remote host, or established a remote session.
That the SMB connections involved unauthorized access, remote execution, or file transfer.
That the LSASS access involved credential extraction or memory reading.
That browser activity uploaded organizational data or otherwise caused data loss.
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate the mstsc UserAssist artifact with process-creation, Prefetch, RDP client, firewall, and network records to determine whether a remote connection occurred and its destination.
Obtain SMB share and file-access auditing for the two connections to DC-HD-01, and determine whether the activity matches expected workstation domain operations.
Identify the svchost service associated with the LSASS access events and review related process and endpoint telemetry.
Validate the ChartMate updater binary and its observed update behavior against the organization's approved software baseline.
Review browser upload or file-transfer telemetry for the docs.google.com activity if data movement is a concern.
